clue.text: Call welcome to a man of letters ?

definitions.meaning: a bugle call sounded at military funerals and at the end of the day

definitions.text: welcome to a man of letters
definitions.meaning: the final delivery of the day is a relief to a postman, whose 'letters' are mail, not literature

explanation.surface: Someone sends greetings to a distinguished author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of letters' suggests a writer; here it is a postman, glad to see the day's final round. In Britain the bugle call of the same name ends the military day.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle call is a signal, and the day's final round of mail would cheer a weary postman.

clue.text: The 21 dn determined by blind fury

definitions.text: The 21 dn determined by blind fury

parts.words: The 21 dn determined by blind fury
parts.note: the span (21 down) of one's existence, cut off by Atropos, the Fate Milton calls 'the blind Fury'

explanation.surface: A prison sentence handed down by an angry judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is STRETCH, which looks like a prison term; here it is the span of a life, which Milton's 'blind Fury' in Lycidas ends by slitting the thread.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole span of a person's existence is the duration the Fates measure out and cut.

clue.text: Sounds like part of the insignia of a Knight Bachelor

indicators.note: the clue says the word spoken resembles another phrase

parts.note: a knight with no order is addressed 'Sir', and a bachelor is single

explanation.surface: A remark about the badge given to a certain kind of knight.
explanation.walkthrough: A Knight Bachelor is a 'Sir' who is 'single', and SIR SINGLE said aloud gives the girth or belt worn as part of a knight's trappings.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcingle is a girth strap round a horse or a belt on a cassock, part of formal trappings.

clue.text: Advertisements for some pastries?

definitions.meaning: cream-filled light pastries are called this

explanation.surface: Asking whether these are adverts for cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotional plugs are blurbs, and light cream-filled cakes share the same name.

clue.text: But his development should not be stunted

definitions.text: But his development should not be stunted

indicators.note: development means the letters grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A learner's growth should never be held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges STUNTED, and the whole clue also describes a learner whose growth must not be stunted.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner at school or college is someone whose growth through education should be encouraged.

clue.text: It's material to enquire after one parent

indicators.note: the asking word is placed after the parent word

parts.note: a dam is a mother, used of animals
to enquire is to ask

explanation.surface: Asking about a mother or father is described as relevant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like 'relevant', but it is the definition: a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven fabric, so it is a material.

clue.text: Decoration not worn with plain-clothes ?

parts.note: a medal suggests itself, but this is any ornament, which plain clothing lacks

explanation.surface: A medal that is left off when off duty in civvies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decoration' suggests a medal; plain clothes are by definition free of any ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament or embellishment is a decoration, the very thing plain clothing lacks.

clue.text: In sibilant terms the plea is reversed

indicators.note: reversed says the run inside is read from right to left
In tells us the letters sit inside the word sibilant

explanation.surface: A hissing defence that gets overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals letters inside SIBILANT, and 'reversed' (at the clue's end, after 'the plea is') says read them backwards: the word backwards is TNALIBIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A defence that one was elsewhere at the time is a plea made in court.

clue.text: Want an attendant? Just ring

definitions.meaning: a custodian or warden who looks after something
a guard ring worn to hold a wedding ring in place

explanation.surface: If you need staff, just call for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a telephone call or bell; it is a guard ring that stops a wedding band slipping off.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian looks after things, and a guard ring holds another band securely on the finger.

clue.text: Lies do upset a princess

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Falsehoods distress a royal lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges LIES DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the Irish princess loved by Tristan in the Arthurian legend.

clue.text: One-time order to put two and two together

definitions.text: One-time order to put two and two together

parts.words: One-time order to put two and two together
parts.note: a former army drill command telling soldiers in pairs to make ranks of four

explanation.surface: An old instruction to work something out by deduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put two and two together' means deduce; here it is literal, men in twos joined into fours on parade, an order no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the drill-sergeant's command for soldiers to regroup from two ranks into four.

clue.text: The girl who can exist on nothing?

indicators.note: the existing word comes on, that is after, the nothing

parts.note: O is the zero shape, nothing
to exist is to live

explanation.surface: A girl so frugal she can survive on no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Essays which are certainly not pointless

definitions.meaning: an essay is an attempt or try
in rugby, scoring touchdowns earns points

explanation.surface: Compositions with a definite purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essays' means attempts, not written compositions; rugby scores of this name earn points, so they are never pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Attempts are efforts, and rugby touchdowns each earn the team points.

clue.text: Flower in a gentle transformation

indicators.note: a transformation changes form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bloom found in some mild change of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformation' rearranges the letters of IN A GENTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweet briar, a wild rose with pink blooms.

clue.text: The bird has flown

parts.note: the idiom for someone escaping, read literally as a bird that travels away with the seasons

explanation.surface: The fugitive has escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bird has flown' is the idiom for a person who has fled; read literally it describes a seasonal traveller among birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird that flies off to another region each season is a seasonal traveller.

clue.text: One of the great men of ancient history

definitions.text: One of the great men of ancient history

parts.words: One of the great men of ancient history
parts.note: the Macedonian king surnamed 'the Great'

explanation.surface: A description of a famous historical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great' is literal: the Macedonian king is known as 'the Great'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Macedonian conqueror is called 'the Great' and lived in the ancient world.

clue.text: Watts provided a physical example of this

definitions.text: Watts provided a physical example of this

parts.words: Watts provided a physical example of this
parts.note: G. F. Watts made the bronze statue titled with this word after 'Physical'; also, a watt is a unit of power

explanation.surface: A scientific remark about units of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watts' suggests units of power; it is the Victorian artist G. F. Watts, whose horse-and-rider statue 'Physical Energy' stands in London's Kensington Gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: The statue's title supplies the word, and in physics vigour of this kind is capacity for doing work.

clue.text: Large marine animal of State importance

parts.note: large means great
a seal is a sea mammal

explanation.surface: A big sea creature treated as a national treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The def is an adjective phrase: the stamp so named is the one used on documents of State importance.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch's official stamp authenticating state documents is used for matters of national weight.

clue.text: One who agrees to invite a beast in

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, a beast
saying 'come in' to a visitor is telling them to enter

explanation.surface: Someone who consents to let an animal into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Inviting a beast in means saying 'Ass, enter!'
explanation.definitionFit: A person who consents is one who gives assent.

clue.text: Hard to miss these models

definitions.meaning: an easy catch or chance, impossible to fail with
people who pose for a painter

explanation.surface: These fashion models are very conspicuous.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, an easy catch or chance in a game is one no one should miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy chances are simple to take, and artists' models pose for portraits.

clue.text: Behind bars it is measured in time, not distance

definitions.text: Behind bars it is measured in time, not distance

parts.words: Behind bars it is measured in time, not distance
parts.note: a word for a length or extent is also slang for a prison term

explanation.surface: In prison, sentences are counted in years.
explanation.walkthrough: The word usually means a length; in prison slang it is a sentence served, so measured in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison term is slang for a period inside, while the word elsewhere means a distance or span.

clue.text: Japanese V.I.P. instructs (pointlessly) in hold-up technique

indicators.note: pointlessly means the compass points west and south are removed

parts.note: to instruct someone is to show them
a robber holds people up with a firearm

explanation.surface: A Japanese dignitary teaches an armed robbery method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' takes the compass points W and S out of SHOWS, leaving SHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was the military ruler of feudal Japan, a very important person.

clue.text: When his queen should have died, said Macbeth

definitions.text: When his queen should have died, said Macbeth

parts.words: When his queen should have died, said Macbeth
parts.note: on hearing of Lady Macbeth's death he says 'She should have died' at a later time

explanation.surface: A question about Shakespeare's tragic king and his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Macbeth's 'She should have died hereafter', meaning at some later time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means at a later time, which is when Macbeth thought his wife ought to have died.

clue.text: Cook a sort of joint

definitions.meaning: to cook meat in an oven
a large piece of meat cooked in the oven

explanation.surface: Prepare meat for the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Oven-cooking is a method of preparing food, and a Sunday joint is a cut of meat so cooked.

clue.text: It is usually taken in water

definitions.text: It is usually taken in water

parts.words: It is usually taken in water
parts.note: suggests medicine swallowed with water, but it is a swim or dip

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to take a medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in water' sounds like a pill swallowed with a drink; one takes a swim in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A swim or dip is something one takes, in the sea or a pool.

clue.text: Profits for kicks

definitions.meaning: an old verb: 'what ... it?' means what does it profit
to kick is to strike with the foot

explanation.surface: Earnings made for thrills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profits' is a verb here, in the archaic sense of 'to boot', to avail.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic verb means avails or benefits, and also strikes with the foot.

clue.text: His interest may sometimes be said to be flagging

definitions.text: His interest may sometimes be said to be flagging

parts.words: His interest may sometimes be said to be flagging
parts.note: the railway official waves flags to send trains off

explanation.surface: Someone whose enthusiasm is waning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flagging' suggests tiring; a British railway official of this name waves a flag to start a train.
explanation.definitionFit: The railway official in charge of a train signals with flags, so his job is waving them.

clue.text: Look-out man ?

parts.note: not a sentry but a person whose attention turns outwards to others

explanation.surface: A sentry keeping watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look-out man' suggests a sentry; it is a person who looks outward, the sociable type.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, sociable person directs attention outwards rather than inwards.

clue.text: The character of a tuner, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that these letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Wondering what sort of person a piano tuner is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of A TUNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's temperament or disposition is their basic character.

clue.text: Evidently a painter of note

parts.note: a famous American painter whose surname also describes someone producing musical notes by blowing through the lips

explanation.surface: Praise for a celebrated artist.
explanation.walkthrough: James McNeill Whistler was a famous painter; his name says he makes notes, hence 'evidently'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American artist bears a surname meaning one who produces tunes through pursed lips.
